prompt: Which of these counts as evidence for a promotion, by the lesson?

choices.text: She works very hard
choices.why: True and irrelevant: effort is not on the ladder.

choices.text: She has been at the company for six years
choices.why: Tenure is deliberately left off the ladder.

choices.text: She is clearly ready
choices.why: “Ready” is the conclusion the case has to reach, not evidence for it.

choices.text: Two other teams adopted her pattern, and say so in writing
choices.why: Right: specific, dated, and confirmed by people outside the team.

prompt: Why do most panels want to see next-level work sustained over six months to a year?

choices.text: Because promotions are only processed once a year at most companies, so the window has to match
choices.why: Cycle timing is not the reason; it is about pattern.

choices.text: To see a pattern
choices.why: Right: one excellent project shows somebody can do it once; a promotion says they do it reliably.

choices.text: To make the person wait
choices.why: Waiting is not the purpose.

choices.text: To collect more praise for the case
choices.why: Praise is not evidence; varied work against different rows is.

prompt: Why did the one-to-one notes matter for Yara’s case?

choices.text: The panel reads them
choices.why: The panel reads the case; the notes are where Renata found the evidence.

choices.text: They are required by Caju’s process
choices.why: No requirement is mentioned.

choices.text: Without them, Renata would have remembered the migration and little else
choices.why: Right: dated notes protect the case from recency and vividness.

choices.text: They contained Yara’s own written statement of why she deserved to be promoted to staff
choices.why: They contained dated observations, not a statement from Yara.

prompt: Match each piece of Yara’s evidence with the staff row it supports.

pairs.left: the booking migration across three teams
the waiting-list design from an ambiguous problem
two teams adopting the reminder pattern
the rollback plan that was used once and worked

prompt: Sorting the evidence shows one row is thin. What does the lesson say a manager must not do?

choices.text: Tell the person which row is thin
choices.why: That is the most useful outcome of the conversation.

choices.text: Send a thin case
choices.why: Right: the panel will have that conversation instead, with less care, and the no will come from strangers.

choices.text: Suggest the kind of work that would fill the gap in that row over the coming months
choices.why: That gives the person a plan, which the lesson recommends.

choices.text: Wait another cycle
choices.why: Waiting with a plan is fine; the failure is sending a case that cannot pass.

prompt: Put the four parts of Caju’s promotion-case template in order.
items: One section per row of the ladder

prompt: Why does the gaps section make a case stronger?
hint: What happens when a panel finds a weakness itself?

choices.text: Panels reward modesty
choices.why: It is about credibility, not modesty.

choices.text: It makes the case longer
choices.why: Length is not the point.

choices.text: A weakness the panel finds itself makes it doubt everything else; one the manager names shows she knows the person
choices.why: Right: naming it first protects the credibility of the rest.

choices.text: It is required by the template
choices.why: It is in the template for a reason, which is the question.

prompt: “Yara is a natural leader who is always willing to help other teams.” What is wrong with it as a case paragraph?

choices.text: It is untrue
choices.why: The lesson says every word was true.

choices.text: It is too short
choices.why: Length is not the problem; checkability is.

choices.text: Nothing in it is checkable; it only tells the panel that Renata likes Yara
choices.why: Right: the rewrite makes a claim about effect, with months, names and links.

choices.text: It should be in the summary
choices.why: It would be as weak there.

prompt: Match each weak phrase with what the lesson suggests instead.

pairs.right: what she did inside the team’s work
evidence of the next level now

prompt: Why do companies use a panel rather than letting each manager decide promotions?

choices.text: Because managers cannot be trusted with anything that touches pay
choices.why: The reason is consistency and bias, not a general distrust of managers.

choices.text: To apply one bar across many managers
choices.why: Right: and to bring in people with no stake, which limits each manager’s biases.

choices.text: To slow promotions down
choices.why: Speed is not the purpose.

choices.text: Because the law requires it
choices.why: No law is mentioned.

prompt: Diego was told “not this time” after his staff case, and nothing else. What did the panel’s actual reasoning turn out to be?

choices.text: He had not been at Caju long enough
choices.why: Tenure is not on the ladder.

choices.text: Deep technical work within Agenda, no influence beyond it
choices.why: Right: specific, against a row, and something he could work on.

choices.text: His code quality was poor
choices.why: The case showed deep technical work; craft was not the gap.

choices.text: There were no staff positions available that cycle, so every case in his batch was refused
choices.why: Nothing says so; the reasoning was about his evidence.

prompt: What does the lesson say a manager must never do after a no?

choices.text: Blame the panel
choices.why: Right: it teaches the process is arbitrary and gives the person nothing to work on.

choices.text: Give the panel’s reasons
choices.why: Giving the reasons is the second part of the conversation.

choices.text: Let the person react
choices.why: Room for their reaction is the fourth part.

choices.text: Describe the work that would change the answer next time, without promising the outcome
choices.why: That is the third part, done correctly.

prompt: At Caju, the manager is not in the room, so the case has to stand on its ___.
hint: Nobody is there to explain it.

prompt: A manager’s case for a promotion to senior says: “He helped with the payments migration, always delivers, and has huge potential.” Which single change would improve it most?

choices.text: Add more praise from the team, so the panel sees how much everybody around him values his work
choices.why: Praise is not evidence; it would make the case warmer and no stronger.

choices.text: Replace each phrase with what he did, when, and the result
choices.why: Right: “helped with”, “always” and “potential” are the weak words; specific dated work replaces all three.

choices.text: Mention his years at the company
choices.why: Tenure is off the ladder.

choices.text: Remove the gaps section
choices.why: There is no gaps section, and removing one would weaken a case.
